## Abstract {.section-header style="background: #e3f2fd;"}

**CuraLit** transforms how researchers interact with scientific literature by enabling the creation of **custom AI assistants** trained on curated PubMed articles. This Rust-based tool filters millions of articles by keywords, generates comprehensive statistics and visualizations, and produces specialized Large Language Models (LLMs) using Ollama. 

**Key Innovation**: Transform 36+ million PubMed articles → Focused corpus → Custom AI research assistant in minutes!

**Advantages**: Memory-efficient, resumable operations, interactive visualizations, easy model sharing, 100% private/local processing.

## System Architecture {.section-header style="background: #f3e5f5;"}

### Components

**1. Search Engine**
- Streaming XML parser
- AND/OR keyword logic
- Checkpoint system
- Parallel processing

**2. Analytics**  
- Statistical analysis
- MeSH term extraction
- Author/journal rankings
- Temporal trends

**3. Visualizations**
- Interactive HTML plots
- Publication timelines
- Topic heatmaps
- Collaboration networks

**4. Model Generation**
- Ollama integration
- Custom prompts
- Local training
- Easy distribution

### Technical Features

🚀 **Performance**
- Memory: ~300MB (constant)
- Speed: 2,400 articles/sec
- Resumable: 100%

🤖 **AI Integration**
- Models: llama3, mistral, phi3
- Privacy: 100% local
- Custom research prompts

📦 **Distribution**
- Formats: tar.gz, zip
- Size: KB-MB (metadata only)
- Sharing: Email, USB, Git

## Quick Start {.section-header style="background: #ffe0b2;"}

### Installation (5 min)
```bash
# Install Rust
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 \
  -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh

# Build CuraLit  
git clone github.com/user/curalit
cargo build --release

# Install UV (Python package manager)
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

### Complete Workflow
```bash
# 1. Search (2-5 min)
curalit search -k "diabetes" \
  -d ./data -o study

# 2. Analyze (10 sec)
curalit stats -c study.csv

# 3. Visualize (30 sec)
uv run study_visualize.py

# 4. Generate (5-10 min)
curalit generate -c study.csv \
  -m diabetes-expert --package

# 5. Create model
ollama create diabetes-expert \
  -f Modelfile_*

# 6. Use it!
ollama run diabetes-expert
```

:::
